newsitem.title: USA: White House hints at NATO announcement on Tuesday.
newsitem.headline: White House hints at NATO announcement on Tuesday.

text.p: White House spokesman Mike McCurry hinted broadly on Friday that President Bill Clinton will make an announcement next Tuesday on plans to expand the North Atlantic Treaty Organisation (NATO) security alliance.

Clinton, who sets off on a four-day campaign trip on Sunday, was likely to make a speech on the subject in Detroit on Tuesday, McCurry told his daily briefing. "If I were picking a place to go I would pick Detroit on Tuesday because he may make some news on foreign policy," McCurry said.

"A little hint: not long ago the president suggested that sometime early in 1997 there should be ... a NATO summit to discuss the very important question of NATO expansion and enlargement. I think he might have some more specifics to talk about on Tuesday when he discusses that subject in Detroit."

Foreign policy has hardly made an appearance in the U.S. presidential campaign, which pits Clinton against Republican nominee Bob Dole. Leading Dole by double digits in most opinion polls ahead of the Nov. 5 election, Clinton may wish to highlight the matter of NATO expansion while on the campaign trail to underline his role as commander-in-chief.

In September, U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher said NATO leaders would hold a summit next year to decide formally on new members and to approve a charter defining the alliance's relationship with Russia.
A preparatory meeting of foreign ministers is expected to be held in Brussels in December.

Russia has long resisted the enlargement of NATO, created as a security alliance to protect western Europe against the former Soviet Union. But Moscow in recent months appears to have become more reconciled to the idea of NATO expansion.
Poland, Hungary and the Czech Republic were generally viewed as first in line to join the alliance on some basis.
